displayQuote: We must use time wisely and forever realize that the time is always ripe to do right

meta.title: Who really said "We must use time wisely and forever realize that the time is always ripe to do right"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not Nelson Mandela. It is a reworded line from Martin Luther King Jr.’s 1963 Letter from Birmingham Jail: “the time is always ripe to do right.”
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'We must use time wisely and forever realize that the time is always ripe to do right'?
meta.ogDescription: A misattribution. It is a garbled version of Martin Luther King Jr.’s line from the 1963 Letter from Birmingham Jail, not a Nelson Mandela quote.

answer.label: Not Nelson Mandela — actually Martin Luther King Jr.
answer.authorDates: 1929–1968 · Baptist minister and civil-rights leader; written 16 April 1963
answer.sourceLine: The line is a slightly reworded version of a sentence from Martin Luther King Jr.’s “Letter from Birmingham Jail” (16 April 1963), whose original text reads “We must use time creatively, in the knowledge that the time is always ripe to do right.” It is not from Nelson Mandela; the Mandela credit is a modern misattribution of a garbled King quotation.

source.heading: Where it really comes from
source.excerpt: Human progress never rolls in on wheels of inevitability; it comes through the tireless efforts of men willing to be co-workers with God, and without this hard work, time itself becomes an ally of the forces of social stagnation. We must use time creatively, in the knowledge that the time is always ripe to do right. Now is the time to make real the promise of democracy…
trail: The sentence appears verbatim in the full text of King’s Letter from Birmingham Jail ↗, dated 16 April 1963.
Study guides trace it to the letter’s passage on the “myth of time,” ending “the time is always ripe to do right” (GradeSaver ↗).
Quote aggregators reproduce the same King line under Nelson Mandela’s name with no source (Goodreads ↗).
source.cutTag: ↑ King wrote “creatively, in the knowledge that” — the Mandela version swaps in “wisely and forever realize”
source.excerptNote: King’s point is that time is neutral: it can serve justice or stagnation, so people must act rather than wait. The circulated Mandela quotation lifts only the second sentence and softens its wording.

source.rightsNote: The wording is Martin Luther King Jr.’s, from a 1963 text still under copyright controlled by the King Estate; it is not public domain. Quote for comment and scholarship with attribution to King.

author.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
author.heading: About the real source
author.bio: Martin Luther King Jr. (1929–1968) was the Baptist minister who led the American civil-rights movement and won the 1964 Nobel Peace Prize. He wrote the “Letter from Birmingham Jail” on 16 April 1963 while jailed for nonviolent protest, answering white clergymen who called his campaign “untimely.” The line about time being “always ripe to do right” is his direct rebuttal to that call for patience.

copyAttribution: Martin Luther King Jr., "Letter from Birmingham Jail," 16 April 1963 — "We must use time creatively, in the knowledge that the time is always ripe to do right." (Often misattributed to Nelson Mandela in reworded form.)

misattribution.heading: The misattribution
misattribution.intro: The quotation circulates widely under Nelson Mandela’s name, usually in the form “We must use time wisely and forever realize that the time is always ripe to do right.” That is a reworded fragment of a King sentence, and no primary Mandela source exists for it.

items.why: Quote sites such as Goodreads ↗ and Quotefancy list “We must use time creatively, and forever realize that the time is always ripe to do right” as Mandela’s, but none cite a speech, book, or letter — and the wording matches King’s 1963 sentence, not any documented Mandela text.

misattribution.truthLine: The words originate with Martin Luther King Jr. in the Letter from Birmingham Jail ↗ (16 April 1963): “We must use time creatively, in the knowledge that the time is always ripe to do right.”

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: King wrote the letter in the margins of a newspaper and on scraps of paper after his arrest during the 1963 Birmingham desegregation campaign. Eight local clergymen had published a statement calling the protests “unwise and untimely” and urging Black residents to wait.

The sentence about time is King’s answer: progress is not automatic, and “the time is always ripe to do right” means there is never a wrong moment to act justly. Stripped of that context and re-credited to Mandela, the line loses its specific argument against the politics of ‘wait.’
context.pull: “The time is always ripe to do right.”
